paper.title: Dynamic prediction of preterm birth and gestational age at delivery based on longitudinal electronic health records.
paper.abstract: This study introduces GestaCare, a deep learning framework designed to jointly optimize all-cause preterm birth (PTB) risk classification and time-to-delivery regression. Using routine electronic health record (EHR) data, the model dynamically updates the estimated remaining weeks at every antenatal visit without requiring specialized assays; together with prospective same-center temporal and prospective external validation, these results suggest that routine EHR data may provide an EHR-based complement to omics-based "pregnancy clock" studies. We develop and validate the framework using a large-scale retrospective cohort covering 14 calendar years (2011-2024), comprising 56,373 singleton and 3577 twin pregnancies. To our knowledge, this represents one of the largest and longest-spanning longitudinal single-center EHR cohorts reported for dynamic PTB prediction. In prospective validation, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC)/area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) values are 0.841/0.478 and 0.785/0.856 in prospective same-center temporal validation and 0.810/0.328 and 0.644/0.686 in prospective external validation for singleton and twin pregnancies, respectively. In prospective external validation, these values correspond to relative AUROC/AUPRC gains of 7.0%/23.3% for singleton pregnancies and 2.7%/2.7% for twin pregnancies over the strongest same-study baselines. Interpretability analysis suggests a data-driven distinction in PTB-associated clinical patterns: predictive signals in singleton pregnancies are characterized by a nutritional-inflammatory dominance (driven by placental-hepatic function and systemic inflammation markers), whereas twin pregnancies exhibit a mechanical-hemodynamic dominance (driven by cervical constraints and cumulative metabolic load). Finally, in a pilot clinician evaluation, obstetricians rate GestaCare explanations as more aligned with clinical knowledge than those from XGBoost with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) (mean clinical alignment score, 4.25/5.00 vs. 3.50/5.00) in a small retrospective assessment.

paper.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based cell death-immune prognostic model for risk stratification in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
paper.abstract:
Background: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) shows marked prognostic heterogeneity, partly driven by interactions between regulated cell death and the tumor immune microenvironment. A framework integrating multiple cell-death programs with immune states is still lacking.
Methods: This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize immune-cell-death interactions in DLBCL. Immune-cell-death-related genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with immune and cell-death gene sets. A cell-death-immune score (CDIS) was constructed using 101 machine-learning combinations and evaluated in three external cohorts. This study assessed immune infiltration, cell-death transcriptional programs, cell-cell communication, ligand-target interactions, pseudotime trajectories, drug connectivity, molecular docking and virtual perturbation. In vitro assays further tested BAFF stimulation and tamoxifen treatment in DLBCL cell lines.
Results: We identified 159 immune-cell-death-related genes and selected 16 genes from 25 candidates to construct the CDIS prognostic model; CoxBoost plus random survival forest ranked highest (mean C-index 0.703). High CDIS was associated with suppressed transcriptional programs of immunogenic cell death and an immune-cold microenvironment with M2-like macrophage enrichment. CDIS provides incremental value over International Prognostic Index (IPI), particularly within the IPI 2 stratum, where it significantly further distinguished high- from low-risk patients (5-year overall survival 63.6% vs. 42.7%; log-rank P = 0.012). Single-cell analysis localized model genes mainly to macrophages and identified an M2-like macrophage-BAFF/APRIL-malignant B-cell axis. Exogenous BAFF promoted DLBCL-cell proliferation and reduced apoptosis, whereas tamoxifen inhibited proliferation dose-dependently.
Conclusions: CDIS serves as a complementary prognostic model to IPI, refining risk within IPI strata, and reveals a candidate mechanism centered on the M2-like macrophage-BAFF/APRIL-malignant B-cell axis.

paper.title: Opportunistic CT sarcopenia screening: multicenter validation of sex-specific T12-to-L3 conversion models.
paper.abstract:
Objectives: Measuring muscle parameters at the third lumbar vertebra (L3) is a standard approach for assessing sarcopenia, but these data are not always available on routine CT scans. The twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12) is a promising surrogate, but reliable conversion formulas are lacking. This study aimed to develop and validate formulas for estimating L3 muscle parameters from T12 measurements.
Materials & Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included a total of 3,698 patients aged ≥ 60 years, comprising a training cohort (n = 3,073), an internal validation cohort (n = 216), and two external validation cohorts (n = 163 and n = 246). Deep learning software was used to quantify skeletal muscle index (SMI), normal-attenuation SMI (NSMI), skeletal muscle density (SMD), and intramuscular adipose tissue percentage (IMAT%) at the T12 and L3 levels. Agreement was evaluated via Bland-Altman analysis and concordance correlation coefficients (CCCs). Sex-specific basic (T12-only) and advanced (incorporating age, body mass index [BMI], and interaction terms) linear regression models were developed, with regression coefficients strictly stabilized utilizing a 1000-iteration bootstrap resampling method.
Results: Significant systematic biases were observed between T12 and L3 measurements (e.g., male SMI bias: -13 cm²/m²), although agreement remained good to excellent (CCCs: 0.82-0.9). The advanced models, incorporating age and BMI, demonstrated high predictive accuracy (training R2: 0.68-0.83) and consistently outperformed basic models in all validation cohorts (all p < 0.001), with NSMI and SMD showing the highest magnitude of improvement.
Conclusions: We developed reliable, sex-specific conversion formulas to estimate L3 muscle parameters from T12 CT images. These validated tools facilitate opportunistic sarcopenia screening from routine CT scans where the L3 vertebra is unavailable, promoting standardized diagnosis and broader clinical application.

paper.title: Machine learning-based prediction of mortality at candidemia diagnosis: development and external validation across multicentre cohorts.
paper.abstract:
Objective: Early identification of candidemia patients at high risk of death may inform clinical management. We aimed to develop and externally validate a clinically interpretable machine learning model to predict 30-day all-cause mortality at candidemia diagnosis.
Methods: The derivation cohort comprised pooled data from three prospective Spanish cohorts including adults with candidemia. Following benchmarking of seven supervised algorithms, an XGBoost algorithm was developed using nested cross-validation. Discrimination was assessed by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR). Calibration was assessed by calibration plots, intercept and slope. Overall performance was assessed by Brier score and scaled Brier score. Model interpretability was evaluated using Shapley additive explanations values. External validation used an international cohort from the European Confederation of Medical Mycology Candida III study.
Results: Among 1,640 patients in the derivation cohort, 476/1,640 (29%) died within 30 days. The final model retained nine predictors of mortality: age, neoplasia, chronic kidney disease, chronic liver disease, recent surgery, septic shock, intensive care unit setting, presumed catheter-related source, and corticosteroid exposure. The derivation AUC-ROC was 0.749 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.723-0.775), AUC-PR 0.562 (95% CI 0.522-0.607), and Brier score 0.171 (95% CI 0.164-0.178). In the external validation cohort (n = 632 patients, 228/632, 36% mortality), AUC-ROC was 0.668 (95% CI 0.628-0.710), AUC-PR 0.515 (95% CI 0.467-0.574), and Brier score 0.218 (95% CI 0.204-0.232). Logistic recalibration improved the Brier score to 0.213 (95% CI 0.203-0.222) without changing discrimination.
Conclusion: This multicentre study developed and externally validated a machine-learning model using routinely available clinical variables that may provide a framework for early risk stratification of 30-day mortality in patients with candidemia. External validation showed lower discrimination and the need for recalibration, supporting further local validation before clinical implementation.

paper.title: Preoperative prediction of microsatellite instability in rectal cancer using multiparametric MRI-derived intratumoral heterogeneity and exploration of biological mechanisms: a multicenter study.
paper.abstract:
Purpose: To develop a machine-learning model combining multiparametric MRI-derived intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scores with clinical features for preoperative prediction of microsatellite instability (MSI) in rectal cancer and to explore MSI-associated molecular features.
Methods: This retrospective study enrolled 464 rectal cancer patients from three centers, including training (n = 198; MSI-H, 26), internal validation (n = 110; MSI-H, 12), and external validation (n = 156; MSI-H, 23) cohorts. Three-dimensional ITH scores were derived from T2WI and DWI. Logistic regression identified independent clinical predictors. Six machine-learning algorithms were used to construct clinical, ITH, and combined models. Performance was assessed using AUCs with 95% confidence intervals, calibration curves, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP. TCGA transcriptomics, PPI analysis, and immunohistochemistry in 10 local samples were used for molecular exploration.
Results: Age, tumor length, location, and N stage were independent predictors. The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.865 (95% CI, 0.828-0.899), 0.839 (95% CI, 0.775-0.895), and 0.785 (95% CI, 0.729-0.835) in training, internal, and external cohorts, respectively. In external validation, it was comparable to the clinical model (AUC = 0.790; BH-adjusted P = 0.076), and the ITH-only model performed poorly (AUC = 0.548). SHAP identified tumor location, T stage, and ITH features as major contributors. Transcriptomics identified 378 differentially expressed genes, and PPI analysis suggested AKT1 as a hub candidate. IHC showed higher AKT1 H-scores in MSS tumors (143.60 ± 26.14 vs. 76.74 ± 38.43; P = 0.008).
Conclusion: The model showed favorable training/internal performance but moderate external performance without clear incremental value. Larger prospective multicenter cohorts are needed. Transcriptomic and pilot IHC analyses suggest possible AKT1 expression differences between MSI-H and MSS rectal cancers.

paper.title: AI-Enabled Echocardiography Identifies Prominent Epicardial Adipose Tissue Associated With an Adverse Cardiometabolic Profile.
paper.abstract:
Background: Excess epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is associated with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic dysfunction, but its assessment has traditionally required advanced imaging.
Objectives: We investigated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled echocardiography could characterize epicardial adiposity and identify residual cardiometabolic risk.
Methods: We developed PanAdipo, a video-based deep learning model in 1,114,441 videos from 28,797 studies across the Yale-New Haven Health System (YNHHS) (2016-2022), using report-derived expert reader labels of prominent EAT (2.3% of studies). PanAdipo was evaluated in 5 testing cohorts: a temporally distinct YNHHS transthoracic echocardiography set (n = 4,588 patients contributing 5,130 studies), an emergency department point-of-care ultrasound cohort (n = 10,957), the geographically distinct MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care, version IV) data set (n = 4,549), the community-based MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) Exam 6 (n = 2,740), as well as in held-out YNHHS patients with paired coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography within 12 months (n = 5,167). Analyses examined discrimination of the report label and of CT-defined high indexed EAT volume, correlation with paired cardiac CT phenotypes, and body mass index (BMI)-adjusted associations with cardiometabolic biomarkers and newly documented metabolic disease.
Results: In the held-out health system test set, PanAdipo identified prominent EAT documented in clinical reports with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.91) across views. Against paired CT-derived measurements, PanAdipo discriminated age- and sex-specific high EAT (EAT / heart volume ≥95th percentile) with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.89-0.92) overall and of 0.91-0.95 within age-sex groups, and correlated more strongly with indexed EAT volume (Spearman ρ = 0.76) than with BMI (Spearman ρ = 0.41; all P < 0.001); PanAdipo alone explained 53% of indexed EAT volume variance vs 23% for age, sex, and BMI combined. In MESA, higher scores were associated with an adverse metabolic profile (higher homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance [β = 0.17 per SD; 95% CI: 0.11-0.22; n = 950]) after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. In exploratory health system cohort analyses, higher scores were associated with newly documented steatotic liver disease (pooled BMI-adjusted HR: 1.33 [95% CI: 1.11-1.59] per SD of log[PanAdipo]) and hyperlipidemia (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.04-1.18), with modest precision (Hartung-Knapp intervals crossed 1).
Conclusions: AI-enabled echocardiography provides a scalable digital biomarker that characterizes prominent epicardial adiposity and is associated with an adverse cardiometabolic profile, highlighting a role for echocardiography in metabolic risk stratification.

paper.title: Generative Deep Learning for Computational Destaining and Restaining of Unregistered Digital Pathology Images.
paper.abstract: Conditional generative adversarial networks (cGANs) have enabled high-fidelity computational staining and destaining of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) in digital pathology whole-slide images (WSI). However, their ability to generalize to out-of-distribution WSIs across institutions without retraining remains insufficiently characterized, limiting scalable clinical translation. Previously developed cGAN models trained on 102 registered prostate core biopsy WSIs from Brigham and Women's Hospital were evaluated on 82 spatially unregistered WSIs from three Stanford University patients. To mitigate domain shift without retraining, a preprocessing pipeline consisting of histogram-based stain normalization for H&E-stained WSIs and channel-wise intensity calibration for unstained WSIs was developed. Because image registration was intentionally omitted for real-world deployment conditions, the reported quantitative results are conservative lower bounds reflecting both model performance and limited spatial alignment. Under these conditions, virtual destaining achieved a Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.854, structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.699, and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 18.41 dB. H&E restaining from computationally destained outputs outperformed direct staining from ground-truth unstained inputs across all metrics (PCC: 0.798 vs. 0.715; SSIM: 0.756 vs. 0.718; PSNR: 20.08 vs. 18.51 dB), suggesting that preprocessing quality may be more limiting than model capacity. Qualitative pathological review indicated that benign glandular structures were more reliably preserved, and malignant glands were often rendered with vessel-like morphologies. These findings support the feasibility of applying cGAN-based computational H&E staining and destaining generative models to external WSI datasets using preprocessing-based adaptation alone, and identify malignant gland preservation for future domain adaptation.
categories: Proc Int Conf Mach Learn Appl

paper.title: Fetal fraction in pregnancy loss reflects maternal-fetal physiologic integration: a prospective cohort study in the Copenhagen Pregnancy Loss Cohort.
paper.abstract:
Study Question: Can maternal biomarkers of maternal-fetal physiologic integration predict the fetal fraction of cell-free DNA in pregnancy loss?
Summary Answer: Maternal organ system biomarkers, including cardiometabolic, hepatic, renal, and thyroid markers, substantially predict fetal fraction in pregnancy loss (Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristics Curve (AUC-ROC) 0.77-0.80), indicating that fetal fraction may reflect integrated maternal-fetal physiology.
What Is Known Already: Fetal fraction, which is the proportion of cell-free DNA in maternal plasma derived from the placenta, increases with gestational age and decreases with higher maternal BMI. Existing prediction models on fetal fraction rely mainly on demographics and placental hormones, and the contribution of broader maternal organ-system biomarkers remains unclear.
Study Design Size Duration: Prospective multi-center cohort study within the Copenhagen Pregnancy Loss study with development cohort (n = 992) from a tertiary university hospital and external validation cohorts from two secondary university hospitals (n = 275 and n = 241). Enrollment was from November 2020 to February 2023.
Participants/Materials Setting Methods: Women ≥18 years with confirmed intrauterine pregnancy loss before 22 weeks at three Danish university hospitals were included. Fetal fraction was estimated from cfDNA sequencing using SeqFF. Six clinical characteristics and 36 biochemistry measurements, selected to reflect physiological domains implicated in placentation including thyroid, renal, lipid, and inflammatory markers, were analyzed using Bayesian Hurdle lognormal regression and gradient boosting models with external validation.
Main Results And The Role Of Chance: In adjusted hurdle models, higher total thyroid hormone levels were associated with adequate fetal fraction (e.g. total triiodothyronine (TT3) Odds Ratio (OR) 2.76 (95% CI 1.31-5.87); total thyroxine (TT4) OR 2.42 (95% CI 1.43-4.29)), while higher levels of creatinine and uric acid were inversely associated (e.g. creatinine OR 0.39 (95% CI 0.17-0.91); uric acid OR 0.47 (95% CI 0.26-0.90)). The magnitude of fetal fraction was additionally associated with HDL cholesterol/total cholesterol ratio, uric acid, and creatinine. A gradient-boosting model achieved AUC-ROC 0.77 in internal cross-validation and 0.80/0.78 in external validation (two secondary university hospitals), with aspartate transaminase (AST)/alanine transaminase (ALT) ratio among the strongest predictors alongside beta subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (βhCG) and gestational age.
Limitations Reasons For Caution: The cross-sectional design and pregnancy loss focus limit inference regarding the directionality between maternal biomarkers, placental health, and fetal fraction. SeqFF-based fetal fraction estimation adds measurement noise versus genotype methods, while our pre-specified biomarker panel limits scope to investigated parameters. Our findings require validation in ongoing pregnancies.
Wider Implications Of The Findings: The findings suggest fetal fraction may reflect maternal-fetal physiologic integration rather than merely a technical quality-control parameter. The associations between fetal fraction and cardiometabolic, thyroid, hepatic, and renal markers suggest that fetal fraction may offer broader insights into maternal physiology and maternal organ system adaptation during pregnancy, influencing cell-free DNA dynamics (reflecting placental shedding, maternal clearance, and dilution). The model enables personalized clinical decision-making regarding cell-free fetal DNA test timing in pregnancy loss and thereby improving the efficiency and success rate of cell-free fetal DNA testing.

paper.title: Interpretable machine learning model for predicting major adverse kidney events within 30 days in critically ill patients with acute pancreatitis: development and validation in multicenter cohorts.
paper.abstract:
Background: Acute kidney injury is a frequent and serious complication of acute pancreatitis (AP), contributing to increased mortality and healthcare burden. Major adverse kidney events within 30 days (MAKE30) constitute a patient-centered composite endpoint for assessing kidney outcomes. However, effective tools for identifying patients at high risk of MAKE30 are lacking. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning model for predicting MAKE30 in critically ill patients with AP.
Methods: Three clinical datasets were used. MIMIC-IV served as the development cohort, and external validation used eICU-CRD and a retrospective cohort from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (AHSWMU). Feature selection combined least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and multivariable logistic regression. Seven machine learning algorithms were used to develop prediction models. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret and visualize the final model.
Results: A total of 1,574 patients with AP from multiple centers were included. Six predictors were selected for model development: serum creatinine, red cell distribution width, albumin, aspartate aminotransferase, vasopressor use, and total bilirubin. The random forest model demonstrated favorable overall performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.863 in the internal validation cohort. Performance was consistent across the two independent external validation cohorts, with AUCs of 0.840 in eICU-CRD and 0.848 in AHSWMU. A web-based clinical risk calculator was developed to facilitate model use in clinical practice.
Conclusion: The model developed in this study exhibited favorable performance and robust generalizability in predicting MAKE30 among critically ill patients with AP, providing reliable digital decision support for early risk stratification and individualized intervention strategies.

paper.title: A machine learning model for predicting early adverse outcomes after surgery in patients with early-onset rectal cancer: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Patients often present at advanced stages of early-onset rectal cancer (EORC), which is becoming more common. Within a year following rectal resection, some patients experience early adverse outcomes (EAO), such as severe complications, recurrence, or death; however, there is currently no validated postoperative risk-stratification tool for this population. Current prognostic models concentrate on individual endpoints rather than the composite adversity spectrum that is pertinent to younger patients because they were mostly established in older cohorts. This work sought to create and externally validate a model for detecting EORC patients at greater risk of EAO using a stacking ensemble machine learning approach with SHAP interpretability in order to guide individualized postoperative surveillance and adjuvant therapy decisions.
Methods: In this two-center retrospective cohort study, 648 EORC patients from Center A (2020-2025) constituted the development cohort and 102 patients from Center B (2024-2025) the external validation cohort. Eleven individual machine learning models and a two-layer stacking ensemble (combining three base learners with logistic regression meta-learner) were trained. Model performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis.
Results: Boruta feature selection identified eleven important predictors, with pathological T stage (pT), lymphovascular invasion (LVI), and pathological TNM stage (pTNM) contributing most to model predictions. The stacking ensemble outperformed all 11 individual models, achieving AUCs of 0.91 (95% CI 0.88-0.93) in the training set, 0.89 (95% CI 0.85-0.94) in the internal validation set, and 0.83 (95% CI 0.76-0.91) in the external validation cohort, with a Brier score of 0.1104 and sustained net benefit on decision curve analysis. An interactive web calculator was deployed for individualized risk assessment.
Conclusion: An interpretable stacking ensemble model integrating SHAP analysis and a web-based calculator showed promising predictive performance for EAO following EORC surgery. Designed for postoperative use once pathology data are available, the model provides a comprehensive risk estimate to guide surveillance intensity and interdisciplinary adjuvant therapy decision-making.

paper.title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for early identification of hypotension associated with renal replacement therapy in ICU patients.
paper.abstract:
Background: Renal replacement therapy (RRT) is essential for critically ill patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), yet hypotension remains its most common complication, increasing the risk of organ hypoperfusion and poor outcomes. No reliable tool currently exists to predict hypotension risk before RRT initiation, particularly one designed for nursing integration. This study aimed to develop and validate a nurse-friendly machine learning model using readily accessible pre-RRT variables to predict the risk of RRT-associated hypotension in ICU patients.
Methods: Data from eligible patients in the MIMIC-IV database were used for model development and internal testing, and an independent Chinese ICU cohort was used for external validation. Candidate predictors were identified through an evidence-informed framework combining meta-analysis factors with prespecified patient and treatment variables. Initial predictors were screened according to clinical relevance and routine availability to ICU nurses before RRT initiation. Final feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression in the training set, followed by the development and validation of multiple machine learning models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to enhance model interpretability, and the final model was implemented as a web-based prototype.
Results: A total of 1,342 patients from the MIMIC-IV database and 133 patients from the external set were included in the analysis. The gradient boosting machine (GBM) demonstrated the most consistent overall performance across all datasets, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.801 in the external set. Key contributors to model output included RRT modality, vasopressor use, mean and systolic blood pressures, age, lactate level, and the interval from ICU admission to RRT initiation. The final model was deployed using the Streamlit framework to demonstrate individualized risk visualization.
Conclusions: The GBM-based model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, nursing applicability, and clinical utility. Designed with a nursing-friendly approach, the model enables early risk stratification and supports proactive hemodynamic management before RRT initiation.
Trial Registration: Not applicable.
